name: Sunflower
grown_as: A tall annual grown from seed. William's library lists 'Giant Single', 1.5 to 3 m: one stem and one huge head. Described here as that type.
habit: One stout, upright, unbranched stem 1.5 to 3 m tall, rough with stiff hairs, about 3 to 5 cm thick at the base. Big leaves all the way up, drooping on their stalks. One very large head at the top.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite in the lowest few pairs, alternate higher up the stem
leaf.outline: Broadly heart-shaped to broadly oval, 10 to 30 cm long, the lower leaves the largest
leaf.base: Heart-shaped or cut straight across, then running briefly down into the stalk
leaf.margin: Coarse, uneven, forward-pointing teeth all round the edge from the base to the tip
leaf.veins: Three strong veins from the base (one midrib and two big side veins), with a net of smaller veins between
leaf.surface: Very rough, like sandpaper, with short stiff hairs on both sides; paler beneath
leaf.stalk: Long, 5 to 20 cm, grooved and hairy; the leaves hang from it

flower.form: A huge flat daisy head: one ring of yellow rays round a very broad dark disc
flower.petals: Not true petals: 30 to 50 ray florets in one or two rows, long, narrow-oval and pointed, flat or slightly twisted
flower.centre: A broad flat disc, a third to half the width of the whole head, packed with hundreds of tiny tubular florets in crossing spirals. Dark brown to purple-brown, opening in rings from the outside in, the open ring dusted yellow with pollen
flower.behind: Several rows of broad green bracts with long, leafy, pointed, hairy tips, showing as a fringe round the back and edge of the head
flower.carried: Alone at the very top of the stem. The young head faces up and turns with the sun; the open head faces sideways (often east) and tilts further down as it gets heavier
flower.size: 20 to 35 cm across in giant types

fruit: The seeds (achenes) fill the whole disc in tight spirals. Each is a flattened tear-drop 1 to 1.5 cm long, striped black and grey-white or all black. The ripe head droops face down, the rays shrivel, the back turns yellow-brown and the bracts dry and curl.
seedling: Two large, thick, smooth, oblong seed leaves with rounded tips on a stout stem, often still wearing the seed case. The first true leaves come as an opposite pair, oval and pointed, rough and finely toothed.
winter: Nothing living: an annual. The dead stalk and head may stand into winter for the birds.

leaf: large heart-shaped leaf with a sharp tip
coarse teeth all round the edge
three main veins from the base
bloom: one ring of long pointed golden-yellow rays
a broad dark brown disc at least a third of the head's width, with a spiral pattern
leafy pointed green bracts showing round the edge
seed: flattened tear-drop seed, pointed at one end
seedling: two thick smooth oblong seed leaves on a stout stem
first pair of rough, opposite, toothed true leaves
young: big heart-shaped leaves on long stalks, opposite low down and alternate above
a single bud at the top wrapped in leafy bracts
flower: one huge head at the top of a single very tall stem
head facing sideways or tilted, not flat to the sky
big drooping heart-shaped leaves all up the stem
seedhead: head bent over and hanging, its face turned down and out, rays shrivelled
the dark face packed with seeds in spirals, seen at a slant
brown dry bracts and browning leaves

look_alikes: Perennial sunflowers (such as Helianthus 'Lemon Queen') and Jerusalem artichoke carry many small heads 5 to 10 cm across with yellow, not dark, discs. Rudbeckia has a raised dark cone and hairy, narrow leaves and is far smaller. Heliopsis has opposite leaves throughout and a yellow-brown cone.
